title: The Chemistry of Fireworks | Science of Colour & Explosions
description:
Fireworks are dazzling, but do you know the real science behind those bursts of colour? In this episode of Pale Blue Thoughts, we explore the chemistry that turns the night sky into a glowing canvas. From the ancient Chinese invention of gunpowder to the modern use of metal salts that create vibrant reds, greens, and yellows—this is the fascinating story of pyrotechnics.

We break down the role of fuel, oxidizers like potassium nitrate and perchlorates, binders, regulators, and colour-producing compounds such as strontium, copper, and sodium. You’ll also learn how sparklers work, why metals like aluminium and magnesium create those shimmering sparks, and the environmental consequences of fireworks—from air pollution and heavy metals to perchlorates contaminating water and the stress they cause animals.

As much as fireworks amaze, they leave behind smoke, debris, and toxins. In a world already choking on pollution, it’s time to rethink our celebrations. Can eco-friendly fireworks and sustainable alternatives keep the magic alive without harming our planet? Let’s find out.

#FireworksScience #ChemistryExplained #EcoFriendlyCelebration #palebluethoughts 

00:00 – Intro: Why Fireworks Dazzle
01:05 – What’s Inside: Fuel, Oxidizer, Binders
03:00 – Colour Chemistry: Strontium, Copper, Sodium
05:00 – Effects & Sparks: Aluminium, Magnesium, Patterns
07:10 – Environmental Impact: Smoke, Metals, Perchlorates
09:20 – Safer Alternatives & Regulation
11:00 – Conclusion
